title: Papyrus asks: a shared source-kind classifier with no feedback yet
description: From Papyrus (PPY-f8ff49), Ryan 2026-11-03. Papyrus wants each new Reference classified on two attributes: evidence level (primary, secondary, aggregation, unknown) and voice (reporting, analysis, opinion, advocacy, promotional, mixed, unknown). Questions: 1. Can a standing classifier run usefully with no human labels, using a decision model and a written definition of each class? 2. Can one classifier be shared across all Papyrus sites, since source kind is not site-specific, with corrections from any site as labels? 3. Two outputs on one item in one decide, or two classifiers? 4. What does Papyrus send and call, and when would it be available? Answer on this ticket; Ryan relays.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Answer to PPY-f8ff49. Short version: yes to all of it, as a new separate Cyclotron with one binding and two outputs. Nothing has been built or changed live. One trap for Papyrus: the same item id cannot go to both Cyclotrons (see 4).

**1. Can it run usefully with no human labels? Yes, with limits.**
The Cyclotron runs on the decision model and question text alone. Each class definition goes in the question text. No priming is needed to decide: priming is a separate operation.
I tried this offline on 20 real items from the Machines on Machines votes, using jev-1.13.0 and draft definitions. All 20 were answered:
- Evidence level: primary 12, secondary 7, aggregation 1.
- Voice: analysis 8, reporting 7, opinion 2, promotional 2, unknown 1.
That shows it works and spreads across classes. It says nothing about accuracy, because there are no labels to score against. I did not read the answers against the articles.
Limits until labels exist: accuracy is unmeasured, and confidence should not be used as a gate because nothing calibrates it. On Machines on Machines relevance, confidence had an AUC of 0.468 against votes. Treat these as descriptive attributes at first, not as hard filters.

**2. One classifier shared across all Papyrus sites? Yes.**
Use one binding, for example `papyrus-source-kind`, used by every site. It must be one binding, not one per site, because a target refuses the same output on two bindings. Corrections from any site become labels for that one classifier, and `editor.site` records which site made each. Votes-count-per-site is not broken: that rule stops a vote crossing to a sibling output, and here there is only one classifier. Only an item's latest label counts, so two sites disagreeing means the last correction wins.
Please record corrections and confirmations both. If reviewers only record mistakes, the labels will skew.

**3. Two outputs in one decide, or two classifiers? Both: they are the same thing here.**
Two classifiers in one Cyclotron are two outputs, each with its own labels, question and fitted model. They share one decide. Measured: in these 20 items, 2 outputs took 20 model calls, about 3,100 input tokens each. In r5, 6 outputs took 14 calls for 14 items. Do not merge them into one 28-class question.
Use a separate Cyclotron instead of adding them to r5, so relevance decisions are not affected. The cost is one extra decide for every Reference.

**4. What Papyrus sends and calls**
- Decide: `POST /machine/decisions` with header `X-Cyclotron-Account`, body `{contractVersion, requestId, payload: {bindings: {"<binding>": "<revision>"}, item: {id, values}}}`. It answers 202 with a `jobId`; read the result at `GET /machine/decisions/{jobId}`. `values` must hold the text field the question reads, and other fields are not restricted.
- Corrections: `POST /machine/bindings/{binding}/operations` with operation `feedback`, as for relevance. Labels are the class names above.
- **The trap:** `register_standing_item` refuses an id that exists in any other item list on the account. That includes the r5 list, even though its error message mentions only priming and evaluation lists. So a Reference id already sent to r5 would be refused here. I read this in the code and have not tried it live. The simple answer is a namespaced id, such as `source-kind:<id>`. Otherwise we change that check, which needs a lab deploy.
- `unknown` is an ordinary class, so Papyrus gets it as a normal answer, not as a failure.

**When:** no new code is needed if Papyrus uses namespaced ids. It needs Ryan's approval of the final class definitions (a criteria write), then the new run, then a change set adding the target to `CYCLOTRON_STANDING_RUNS`, which Ryan also approves. After those approvals it is a short job, and Papyrus gets the binding name and revision from us.

**Not yet true:**
- Corrections will be recorded, but nothing retrains from them until the retraining epic (decision-flywheel-1700b73d) is live. Multi-class selection exists in the engine (macro F1) but has not run on a hosted run.
- The worker runs at most 2 commands at a time, shared with relevance. Check the combined volume with the paper monitors before enabling this for every Reference. That check is still open with Papyrus.
